A0001.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (32 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase: In RSO units rent may be raised once every 12 months by the annual allowable percentage published by LAHD (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). Since the formula change no extra percentage for utilities or for an added dependent is allowed; rent resets to market only after a vacancy such as a voluntary move-out or buyout. Key figure: LAHD annual allowable %, once per 12 months (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30); no utility or dependent add-on. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (32 units and built in 1927) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Flagged for human review: Two published effective dates for the new RSO formula: 2026-02-02 per LAHD (D041, D042, official, kept) and 2026-01-24 per a landlord association (reported in docs/starter_README.md section 9; that source is not in the corpus). Human review needed. Source: L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units: A landlord may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault reason (non-payment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew, denying access, unapproved subtenant) or no-fault reason (owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition or removal from the market, government order, conversion), and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions ($11,000 to $27,400 per unit for 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). Key figure: just cause required; no-fault relocation $11,000 to $27,400 (2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles RSO interest on security deposits: Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits, monthly or yearly, as a direct payment or rent credit, and tell the tenant in writing which method they use. The City sets the rate each year. Key figure: annual interest on RSO security deposits (rate set yearly by LAHD). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (built in 1927) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: L.A.M.C. § 151.06.02. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles ban on source-of-income (Section 8) discrimination: Anyone renting housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent or renew, evict, set different terms, or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Tenants can sue for damages and use a violation as a defense to eviction. Key figure: no refusal or different terms based on source of income (vouchers, rental assistance). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. §§ 45.65 to 45.69. Not legal advice.

A0055.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: San Francisco Rent Ordinance (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance) (San Francisco, CA, S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37). For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (Section 37.9) (San Francisco, CA, S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (40 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (built in 1964) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: L.A.M.C. § 151.06.02. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles ban on source-of-income (Section 8) discrimination: Anyone renting housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent or renew, evict, set different terms, or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Tenants can sue for damages and use a violation as a defense to eviction. Key figure: no refusal or different terms based on source of income (vouchers, rental assistance). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. §§ 45.65 to 45.69. Not legal advice.

A0128.explanation: State bar on local rent control (M.G.L. c.40P s.4): Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, so there is no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge. Massachusetts also has no statewide rent cap. Key figure: Local rent control prohibited; no statewide cap. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.40P § 4. Not legal advice.

Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B): A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit. Key figure: 1 month's rent. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2): A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged. Key figure: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.112 § 87DDD½. Not legal advice.

Limit on upfront charges (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b)): At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent may charge only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed. Key figure: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

A0162.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (24 units and built in 1987) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (24 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units: A landlord may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault reason (non-payment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew, denying access, unapproved subtenant) or no-fault reason (owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition or removal from the market, government order, conversion), and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions ($11,000 to $27,400 per unit for 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). Key figure: just cause required; no-fault relocation $11,000 to $27,400 (2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles ban on source-of-income (Section 8) discrimination: Anyone renting housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent or renew, evict, set different terms, or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Tenants can sue for damages and use a violation as a defense to eviction. Key figure: no refusal or different terms based on source of income (vouchers, rental assistance). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. §§ 45.65 to 45.69. Not legal advice.

For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (9 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. §§ 45.65 to 45.69. Not legal advice.

This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. What you could check: the number of units (county assessor records, or the landlord); other facts such as whether the owner lives in the building or whether a special exemption was granted (the landlord or the city housing office can say). Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (Section 37.9) (San Francisco, CA, S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9). A0272.explanation: State bar on local rent control (M.G.L. c.40P s.4): Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, so there is no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge. Massachusetts also has no statewide rent cap. Key figure: Local rent control prohibited; no statewide cap. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.40P § 4. Not legal advice.

Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B): A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit. Key figure: 1 month's rent. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2): A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged. Key figure: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.112 § 87DDD½. Not legal advice.

Limit on upfront charges (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b)): At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent may charge only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed. Key figure: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

A0303.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: the year the building was built. What you could check: when the building was built or first occupied (county assessor or the city rent board). Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: the year the building was built. What you could check: when the building was built or first occupied (county assessor or the city rent board). Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (7 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Tenant Protection Ordinance), just cause and relocation: A landlord may not end a tenancy without an at-fault or no-fault just cause. For a no-fault termination the landlord must pay two months' rent (three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled), or waive that much rent, regardless of income or tenancy length. Key figure: just cause required; no-fault relocation 2 months' rent (3 months for senior or disabled). We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: the year the building was built. What you could check: when the building was built or first occupied (county assessor or the city rent board). Source: S.D.M.C. §§ 98.0701 to 98.0710. Not legal advice.

San Diego prohibition of source-of-income discrimination: Landlords may not refuse to rent or renew, end a tenancy, or set different terms because of a person's source of income, including any rental assistance, vouchers or subsidy, and income standards must count all of a tenant's income and the combined income of co-tenants and cosigners. Key figure: no refusal or different terms based on source of income, incl. any rental assistance. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in San Diego, CA. Source: S.D.M.C. §§ 98.0801 to 98.0806. Not legal advice.

San Diego Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing (Division 11): No one may sell, license or provide to a landlord, and no landlord may use, software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords to recommend rents or occupancy levels. A tenant can sue for an injunction, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation. Key figure: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in San Diego, CA. Source: S.D.M.C. §§ 98.1101 to 98.1104. Not legal advice.

Massachusetts also has no statewide rent cap. Key figure: Local rent control prohibited; no statewide cap. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.40P § 4. Not legal advice.

Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B): A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit. Key figure: 1 month's rent. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2): A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged. Key figure: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.112 § 87DDD½. Not legal advice.

Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed. Key figure: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

A0309.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (6 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Key figure: just cause required; no-fault relocation 2 months' rent (3 months for senior or disabled). We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: the year the building was built. What you could check: when the building was built or first occupied (county assessor or the city rent board). Source: S.D.M.C. §§ 98.0701 to 98.0710. Not legal advice.

San Diego prohibition of source-of-income discrimination: Landlords may not refuse to rent or renew, end a tenancy, or set different terms because of a person's source of income, including any rental assistance, vouchers or subsidy, and income standards must count all of a tenant's income and the combined income of co-tenants and cosigners. Key figure: no refusal or different terms based on source of income, incl. any rental assistance. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in San Diego, CA. Source: S.D.M.C. §§ 98.0801 to 98.0806. Not legal advice.

San Diego Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing (Division 11): No one may sell, license or provide to a landlord, and no landlord may use, software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords to recommend rents or occupancy levels. A tenant can sue for an injunction, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation. Key figure: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in San Diego, CA. Source: S.D.M.C. §§ 98.1101 to 98.1104. Not legal advice.

A0421.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (6 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase: In RSO units rent may be raised once every 12 months by the annual allowable percentage published by LAHD (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). Since the formula change no extra percentage for utilities or for an added dependent is allowed; rent resets to market only after a vacancy such as a voluntary move-out or buyout. Key figure: LAHD annual allowable %, once per 12 months (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30); no utility or dependent add-on. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (6 units and built in 1964) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Key figure: just cause required; no-fault relocation $11,000 to $27,400 (2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq. Not legal advice.

The City sets the rate each year. Key figure: annual interest on RSO security deposits (rate set yearly by LAHD). Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B): A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit. Key figure: 1 month's rent. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

Key figure: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.112 § 87DDD½. Not legal advice.

Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

A0451.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (8 units and built in 1989) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (8 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

Los Angeles ban on source-of-income (Section 8) discrimination: Anyone renting housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent or renew, evict, set different terms, or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Tenants can sue for damages and use a violation as a defense to eviction. Key figure: no refusal or different terms based on source of income (vouchers, rental assistance). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. §§ 45.65 to 45.69. Not legal advice.

A0453.explanation: State bar on local rent control (M.G.L. c.40P s.4): Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, so there is no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge. Massachusetts also has no statewide rent cap. Key figure: Local rent control prohibited; no statewide cap. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.40P § 4. Not legal advice.

Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B): A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit. Key figure: 1 month's rent. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2): A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged. Key figure: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.112 § 87DDD½. Not legal advice.

Limit on upfront charges (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b)): At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent may charge only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed. Key figure: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. A0458.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. A0473.explanation: State bar on local rent control (M.G.L. c.40P s.4): Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, so there is no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge. Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B): A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit. Key figure: 1 month's rent. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2): A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged. Key figure: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.112 § 87DDD½. Not legal advice.

Limit on upfront charges (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b)): At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent may charge only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed. Key figure: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in MA. Source: M.G.L. c.186 § 15B. Not legal advice.

A0474.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.
