The deposit must be held in a New Jersey interest-bearing account, interest belongs to the tenant, and it must be returned with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Key figure: 1.5 months' rent. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units and the tenant has not invoked the law by 30 days written notice; the number of units in the building. The property class suggests at least 5 units, but the unit count itself is not in the data, so we do not rely on it. What you could check: the number of units (county assessor records, or the landlord); other facts such as whether the owner lives in the building or whether a special exemption was granted (the landlord or the city housing office can say). Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2. Not legal advice.

Residential rental application fee cap: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to rent a home; the cap is adjusted each January 1 by CPI. Violations carry penalties and the overcharge is returned to the applicant. Key figure: $50 cap, CPI-adjusted yearly. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: the number of units in the building. The property class suggests at least 5 units, but the unit count itself is not in the data, so we do not rely on it. What you could check: the number of units (county assessor records, or the landlord). Source: P.L.2025, c.405. Not legal advice.

NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income: A landlord may not refuse to rent or treat an applicant differently because of the source of lawful income or rent payment, such as a Section 8 voucher. A landlord may still refuse for insufficient income or poor credit. Key figure: Source of lawful income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is a protected basis. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: owner occupies the other unit of a two-family dwelling, or rents rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; the number of units in the building. The property class suggests at least 5 units, but the unit count itself is not in the data, so we do not rely on it. What you could check: the number of units (county assessor records, or the landlord); other facts such as whether the owner lives in the building or whether a special exemption was granted (the landlord or the city housing office can say). Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-12. Not legal advice.

Fair Chance in Housing Act: Landlords may not ask about criminal history on an application or before making a conditional offer. After the offer they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, must do an individualized assessment, and must give written reasons if they withdraw the offer. Key figure: No criminal-record inquiry before a conditional offer; lookback 6 years (1st degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd degree), 1 year (4th degree); penalties up to $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: owner-occupied premises; the number of units in the building. The property class suggests at least 5 units, but the unit count itself is not in the data, so we do not rely on it. What you could check: the number of units (county assessor records, or the landlord); other facts such as whether the owner lives in the building or whether a special exemption was granted (the landlord or the city housing office can say). Source: P.L.2021, c.110. Not legal advice.

Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act: From July 1, 2027, landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's rent-setting service that pools competitors' nonpublic data or sets rents, lease terms or occupancy by algorithm, and no one may perform that coordinating function. Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act. Key figure: Ban on algorithmic coordination of rents, lease terms or occupancy using competitors' nonpublic data; effective 2027-07-01. This rule is not yet in effect as of 2026-10-01: it takes effect on 2027-07-01. Source: P.L.2026, c.43. Not legal advice.

Newark Rent Control Ordinance: At lease renewal a Newark landlord may not raise rent by more than the CPI-U change over the prior 15 to 3 months, and never more than 4%, once per 12 months, with 30 days written notice. No increase is allowed if the dwelling is not in substantial code compliance or not registered. Key figure: CPI-U change, max 4% per 12 months. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: the year the building was built; Rent Control Board certification of newly constructed multiple dwelling exemption (19:2-18.1). What you could check: when the building was built or first occupied (county assessor or the city rent board); other facts such as whether the owner lives in the building or whether a special exemption was granted (the landlord or the city housing office can say). Source: Newark Mun. Code § 19:2-3. Not legal advice.

Newark Ban the Box housing ordinance: Landlords and brokers may check criminal history only after a formal application, with notice and consent, and may look back only 8 years for indictable convictions or 5 years for disorderly persons offenses (plus listed serious offenses and pending charges). Arrests without conviction, expunged and juvenile records may not be used, and denials need written reasons. Key figure: Criminal history inquiry only after a formal application; 8-year / 5-year lookback; fines up to $500 first, $1,000 repeat. We cannot tell yet whether this rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01. It depends on facts we do not have: owner occupies the other unit of a two-family dwelling, or rents rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; the number of units in the building. The property class suggests at least 5 units, but the unit count itself is not in the data, so we do not rely on it. What you could check: the number of units (county assessor records, or the landlord); other facts such as whether the owner lives in the building or whether a special exemption was granted (the landlord or the city housing office can say). Source: Newark Mun. Code § 2:31-1 et seq. Not legal advice.

A0499.explanation: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (Civ. Code 1947.12, SB 567 version): Rent cannot be raised more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments. A new tenancy may start at any rent. Key figure: 5% + CPI, max 10%. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Not legal advice.

Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction (Civ. Code 1946.2, AB 1529 version): After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (24 months if an adult tenant was added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For a no-fault cause the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent. Key figure: just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault. Another rule takes precedence at this address as of 2026-10-01: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units (Los Angeles, CA, L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq.). This rule yields to it and does not govern here. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2. Not legal advice.

Security deposit cap of one month's rent (Civ. Code 1950.5 as amended by AB 12): A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent; a qualifying small landlord may take up to two months. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out. Key figure: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5. Not legal advice.

Application screening fee cap (Civ. Code 1950.6): A landlord may charge an application screening fee only for actual out-of-pocket screening costs, never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998, and only when a unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and either process applications first-come or refund applicants not selected. Key figure: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6. Not legal advice.

FEHA housing discrimination: source of income, including vouchers (Gov. Code 12955, SB 329 / SB 267): Owners may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers (since SB 329, 2020-01-01), and since SB 267 (2024-01-01) must offer an alternative to credit history when there is a rent subsidy. CRD guidance adds that blanket criminal-history bans are unlawful and arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records may not be considered. Key figure: source-of-income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) discrimination barred; no blanket criminal-history bans. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (33 units) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 329). Not legal advice.

Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 and SB 763): It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set a price) as part of a price-fixing agreement, or while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Not limited to housing; covers shared rent-setting software. SB 763 raised penalties, including civil fines up to $1 million in AG or district attorney actions. Key figure: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data; civil fines up to $1 million. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in CA. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325; SB 763). Not legal advice.

Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable increase: In RSO units rent may be raised once every 12 months by the annual allowable percentage published by LAHD (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). Since the formula change no extra percentage for utilities or for an added dependent is allowed; rent resets to market only after a vacancy such as a voluntary move-out or buyout. Key figure: LAHD annual allowable %, once per 12 months (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30); no utility or dependent add-on. This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (33 units and built in 1962) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Flagged for human review: Two published effective dates for the new RSO formula: 2026-02-02 per LAHD (D041, D042, official, kept) and 2026-01-24 per a landlord association (reported in docs/starter_README.md section 9; that source is not in the corpus). Human review needed. Source: L.A.M.C. § 151.00 et seq. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), with RSO just cause for RSO units: A landlord may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault reason (non-payment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew, denying access, unapproved subtenant) or no-fault reason (owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition or removal from the market, government order, conversion), and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions ($11,000 to $27,400 per unit for 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). Key figure: just cause required; no-fault relocation $11,000 to $27,400 (2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. § 165.00 et seq. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles RSO interest on security deposits: Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits, monthly or yearly, as a direct payment or rent credit, and tell the tenant in writing which method they use. The City sets the rate each year. Key figure: annual interest on RSO security deposits (rate set yearly by LAHD). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: the building facts we have (built in 1962) meet its coverage conditions and none of its exemptions applies. Source: L.A.M.C. § 151.06.02. Not legal advice.

Los Angeles ban on source-of-income (Section 8) discrimination: Anyone renting housing in Los Angeles may not refuse to rent or renew, evict, set different terms, or advertise a preference based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Tenants can sue for damages and use a violation as a defense to eviction. Key figure: no refusal or different terms based on source of income (vouchers, rental assistance). This rule applies to this address as of 2026-10-01: it covers residential rentals in Los Angeles, CA. Source: L.A.M.C. §§ 45.65 to 45.69. Not legal advice.
